newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truckers let 200 trucks leave for Britain.
newsitem.headline: French truckers let 200 trucks leave for Britain.

text.p: Striking French truckers agreed on Thursday to lift their blockade of the Channel port of Calais temporarily to let 200 stranded truck drivers embark for Britain, a spokesman for the port's Chamber of Commerce said.

He said 200 foreign trucks, mainly British, would be allowed to board ferries for Dover. But truckers coming from Britain and stranded by the 11-day-old French drivers' blockade would not be allowed to drive into France.
Britain says at least 1,000 British trucks are stranded in France by the strikers' roadblocks. French truckers maintained almost 250 barricades on main roads and around fuel depots.

David Higginbottom, general secretary of Britain's United Road Transport Union, had said on Wednesday the French truckers had agreed in principle to allow their British colleagues to return home on humanitarian grounds.
With the impact of the strike compounded by a fire in the Channel Tunnel which links Britain to continental Europe, British supermarkets have started airlifting in fresh produce.
The strikers voted to keep up their 11-day stranglehold on the French economy on Thursday, defying government calls to return to work after talks with bosses collapsed over pay demands.
